findings.message: Glossary clash on 'working hours': docs/glossary/time-selection.md already defines **Day period** as 'night (22:00–07:00), morning (07:00–09:00), working hours (09:00–18:00), evening' (DayPeriod.WORK). The change adds a separate glossary term **Working hours** (user's range, settings.md, task 1.1), and its MODIFIED deltas still call the day period 'working hours' (time-selection 'Day-period colours': 'working hours from 09:00 to 18:00'; grid-view 'Hour cell colour': 'night, morning, working hours, evening', scenario '9–17 working hours', 'the working-hours colour'). Task 1.1 only adds '*Not:* the working hours' to Day period, whose entry still lists 'working hours' as one of its periods. glossary.md: 'Every term names one concept'; antipatterns.md: 'Synonym names — naming a glossary concept with another word'. Rename the day period (e.g. 'work period') in the glossary entry and in the deltas, or otherwise make sure one term names one concept.

UX4 ('The non-working grey is calm and lighter than any day-period colour in the light theme') contradicts design D6: the light grey #e4e4e7 has a relative luminance of about 0.777, darker than the existing --color-day-working #f8e6a6 (about 0.793). Task 6.1's tokens.test.ts checks only contrast and 'differs from the accent', so no automated test covers UX4. Pick a grey that meets UX4 (or restate UX4) and add the lightness assertion to tokens.test.ts.

Design D4 and task 6.2 say a single colour stop 'draws a single colour' through buildDayTrackGradient (Plain tracks; Working-hours tracks with no edge, e.g. Moscow on Saturday '0 non-working'). The current builder (src/views/shared/dayTrackGradient.ts) would emit 'linear-gradient(to right, var(--color-accent) 0%)'. CSS Images Level 3 requires at least two colour stops, so engines at the ADR-0009 Safari 12 level drop the declaration and the track loses its colour. Emit two stops (0% and 100%) or a plain background colour for a single stop, and cover it with a test that does not rely on jsdom.

Success metrics are not fully covered by the planned tests: M1 promises '3 of 3 day colourings can be chosen, are restored after a reload and are applied in a second tab (unit BDD)', but the storage scenarios in the settings delta (task 8.4) only reload Working hours and only sync Plain between tabs; no scenario or task checks all three. M4 counts 3 settings-page axe-core runs ('light, dark, and light with the hint shown'), while the spec scenario 'Size, focus and no violations' is an outline over light and dark that also checks 'with the hint shown', i.e. 4 runs. Align the metrics with the scenarios.

findings.message: Incomplete rename of the day period 'working hours' → 'work'. The proposal (What Changes, glossary changed terms) renames the third day period to 'work' and adds 'working hours' to its *Never:* list. The modified grid-view 'Hour cell colour' scenarios already say '9–17 work' and 'the work colour'. `.claude/rules/glossary.md` says: "Renaming the concept means renaming the code, specs and translations in the same change" and "Words listed under *Never:* must not appear for that concept in code, comments, specs, docs". Yet no task renames the existing Gherkin and steps that still name the period 'working hours': `src/test/features/grid_view/grid_view_hour_cells_unit.feature:29` with `steps/grid_view_hour_cells_unit.steps.tsx:61` ('9-17 working hours'), and `grid_view_hour_cells_e2e.feature:20,23` with `steps/grid_view_hour_cells_e2e.steps.ts:42,97` ('working hours and evening colours', 'the working hours cell'). Task 7.2 even expects `grid_view_hour_cells_unit.steps.tsx` to pass unchanged, so the executable features would disagree with the modified spec. The verification greps miss it: task 10.3 covers only `src/locales src/views src/presenter src/app`, not `src/test/features`, and task 1.2's grep does not catch '15 minutes around working hours' in the 'Day-period colors' row of `docs/architecture/views.md:86`. Fix: add the feature, step and doc renames to a task (for example 6.1 or 7.2), and extend the Never-word grep to `src/test/features` and to that docs line.
